item.text: {"claim_count":79,"content_failure_reasons":["The A2 statement that paragraph 63 specifically attributes the fall in excise revenue from 1.5% to 0.3% of GDP to retail fuel-price smoothing overstates the source; the paragraph identifies a sizeable budget cost but does not explicitly link it to that table-row change.","E3 incorrectly says Figures 6, 7, and 11 all compare Mexico with the stated LA-6 and emerging-market peer groups. Figure 6 instead covers available emerging-market economies generally, while the named peer-group composition is supplied in Figure 7; Figure 11 shows LAC6 but does not reproduce that composition.","Decisive chapter evidence is omitted from the substantive map, especially paragraph 55 on sector-specific regulatory barriers, corruption-prone licensing and permitting, and the independence of the competition authority."],"content_usable":false,"material_omission":true,"material_omission_explanation":"The map omits direct evidence material to chapter lenses, most importantly paragraph 55's findings on FDI restrictions, licensing and permit procedures, corruption vulnerabilities, and competition-authority independence, which are decisive for the business-regulation and regulatory-governance questions. It also omits useful qualifications from paragraphs 45–46, 49, 65, and 68 concerning regional inequality, supply-side priorities, Pemex restructuring, exchange-rate shock absorption, and financial inclusion. The paragraph 55 omission is decisive enough to make the content unusable as a chapter-complete source map.","schema_version":"reader_content_audit_v1","source_id":"MAC-010","supported_claim_count":77,"unsupported_claim_count":2,"usable_locator_count":79}
